subject: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny

messages.author: 782ed6ec348dba9b
messages.subject: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny
parts:
I have a data.frame,topTen, with 300,000 rows which includes  a character field, thedate, which I wish  to subset on        

When I run this code in plain R it takes less than a 1/10th of a second
      theWeek <- "2013-09-08"
               
               print(Sys.time())   "2013-09-09 10:25:44.860184 PDT"
               example <- subset(topTen,thedate==theWeek)
               print(Sys.time())  "2013-09-09 10:25:44.90719 PDT"

However, if I run the same code in shiny,in say a reactive expression, it takes between 6 and 7 seconds

Any way I can speed this up?

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny
parts:
You should probably avoid the subset() function, because it uses non-standard evaluation of its arguments. From ?subset:
"This is a convenience function intended for use interactively. For programming it is better to use the standard subsetting functions like [, and in particular the non-standard evaluation of argument subset can have unanticipated consequences."

That said, the use of subset() instead of [ is probably not the source of the performance problem. There are a number of other things that happen in Shiny - for example, if you're sending a big table from the server to the browser, it needs to be converted to JSON and sent over the network.

If you put those print(Sys.time()) lines directly around the subset() call in your shiny app (and monitor the printed output at the R console), what's the time difference?

-Winston

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny
parts:
I am pretty sure the culprit is toJSON. Shiny uses RJSONIO to convert to JSON, and you can speed it up by a considerable factor using rjson. However, rjson is currently lacking a lot of functionality, which is probably the reason RJSONIO is preferred (I use it in rCharts as well for the same reason).

R needs a really fast JSON converter. Maybe using Rcpp?

messages.subject: Re: Slow processing time for subsetting in Shiny
parts:
Hi Winston, 

Very Interesting. We should chat more.

We tried switching to rjson in rCharts and it lead to a huge performance gain. However, rjson only works with some of the JS libraries in rCharts, as the others require more elaborate data structures, which are provided only by RJSONIO.

Maybe, there is a strong use case now to either enhance rjson to provide the same functionality as RJSONIO, or improve RJSONIO to match the speed of rjson.

Alternately, there might be some fast C++ libraries that can be wrapped using Rcpp.

I would be happy to discuss more.

Cheers,
R
